Subject: Post-call: procurement path, budget owner & marketplace interest (NovaPulse)

Hi Alex — thanks for the call today. Quick recap and next steps so we don’t miss anything in procurement:  

1) Procurement path
  - You said purchase > $10k typically goes on a PO; card OK under $10k. Confirm?
  - Marketplace interest: you mentioned possible procurement via AWS Marketplace but need procurement/finance approval for SaaS Marketplace purchases.

2) Docs & requirements you flagged
  - Signed vendor form + W‑9
  - SOW or short statement of work for professional services (if any)
  - Proof of insurance for enterprise contracts (we can provide ACORD)

3) Budget and signatory roster
  - Can you confirm the budget owner and finance sponsor (name/email)?
  - Who signs at final stage (CFO/VP Finance)? Any delegated signatory thresholds?

4) Next steps (proposed)
  - I’ll upload a short procurement checklist and draft quote for your review (attached).
  - Sergio to coordinate commercial terms/discounting if needed.
  - Let’s schedule a 30m procurement sync with the budget owner and signatory on your side.

Attachments: MAL-Procurement-Checklist.pdf (stapled checklist for vendor intake)

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a draft quote by EOD.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com | (415) 555-0182

Hi Rachel — thanks for the summary. Correct on most counts; a few specifics from our side:  

- PO vs Card: we route anything over $10,000 to AP and issue a PO. Smaller purchases are typically placed on a corporate card. Annual subscriptions that will be invoiced annually are usually PO'd.

- Marketplace: we prefer AWS Marketplace for product visibility and internal chargeback, but procurement will only use Marketplace if the SKU and SaaS contract terms match what we need. If Redwood can publish a Merchant of Record offering and provide an AWS Marketplace listing, that will speed internal approvals.

- Required paperwork: vendor form (attached), W‑9 (we need yours), and any SOC/attestation summary for data handling. We will also need a short SOW for services (if Redwood will do onboarding work).

- Budget owner: Emma Liu (emma.liu@novapulse.com) — Director, AI Platform (she owns the budget line).
- Finance sponsor / approver: Thomas Reed (thomas.reed@novapulse.com) — VP Finance (signs for $50k+).
- Delegated signers: Procurement can accept signature from Director-level up to $25k; beyond that needs VP or CFO.

I attached our standard vendor intake (novapulse-po-template.docx).  

We can do a procurement sync next week; availability Tues/Wed afternoons PT.

— Alex

Alex — great detail, appreciate it. A couple quick clarifying items from the Redwood commercial side:  

- Billing cadence: we can invoice annually or quarterly. For PO workflows we typically issue a consolidated annual invoice and support net-30 terms; if you need consolidated monthly billing that’s also possible (we’ll note options in the quote).
- Marketplace: we do support AWS Marketplace (MOR or SaaS) — publishing is a separate enablement step; we can share timeline and what’s required on your end (principal contacts for integration).
- Required legal items: we can provide SOC2 summary, W‑9, and standard Redwood MSA (redline-friendly). If you need proof of insurance, I’ll attach ACORD as requested.

I’ve attached a draft quote for the proposed configuration and a short procurement checklist populated with NovaPulse values (draft-quote-novapulse-Redwood-Std-20260708.pdf). Please review and flag anything missing.

Proposed next step: 30m procurement intake with Emma + Thomas to confirm PO timing and signatory path. Rachel — can you propose 2 time slots next Tue/Wed?

Thanks,
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
